lane_impact: L1 world-exploration: a latent bug in the original world generator, not a design choice. Because rnd() returns [0,1), rand(3) is confined to {0,1,2}. A faithful 1:1 port must decide explicitly whether to reproduce the bug (always 1 exit) or the evident intent (sometimes 2) - and must say which. Worth checking the sibling getSouth/East/WestExits for the same pattern.
text: TerritoryData.getNorthExits contains a dead branch: rng.rand(3) can only return 0, 1 or 2, but the code tests dice == 3 to set count = 2 - so every territory generates exactly one north exit.

lane_impact: L1 world-exploration (removes a fabricated rule from the AP claim) and L6 art-anim-audio-feel (adds a real, uncatalogued one). text: AP == 0 in adventure mode is not a death or retreat condition - it swaps the player to a TIRED idle animation, and the same branch fires in combat at HP <= 25% of max.

lane_impact: L1 world-exploration: corrects the journal's farming-tables claim, which states a 15-minute grace before ROT across all four crop tiers. Three of four. The 12-hour crop is the safe overnight plant — it cannot be lost to inattention, which is a deliberate free-to-play design choice and exactly the kind of feel rule a port would silently get wrong if it applied the grace uniformly.
text: The 12-hour crop has no ROTTED state — its state machine is two-way (PLANTED, then READYFORHARVEST forever), unlike the 15-minute, 1-hour and 6-hour crops which all rot after a 900-second grace.

lane_impact: L1 world-exploration: corrects world-exploration/farming-tables, which states all four tiers carry 'a 15-minute harvest grace before ROT'. Cases 1, 2 and 3 do (900/3600/21600 s + 900 s grace, else ROTTED); case 4 does not. Any ported farming.ts must special-case the 12 h crop as non-perishable, or it will destroy player crops the OG never destroyed.
text: The 15-minute harvest grace does not apply to the 12-hour crop: Obj_VegePatch's case 4 has no grace or ROTTED branch at all, so a 12-hour crop sits in READYFORHARVEST indefinitely.

lane_impact: L1 world-exploration: a porting hazard against world-exploration/place-name-reproduced-from-payload, logged as a lead because it rests on constant-pool adjacency rather than a quoted line of code. Evidence for: NameGenerator.as:136-144 hardcodes exactly two exceptions ('Ibamaya' for territoryID 1405272, 'Gokura' for 1524045), neither of which appears in 89_NameGenerator_PlaceNames.bin; the WEB payload's constant pool carries three capitalised place names adjacently at payload.xml:119264-119266 -- Ibamaya, Gokura, Iwakuni -- immediately after the nameending array and the 'replace' token used only by the name functions; and grep -rn Iwakuni over all 559 android classes returns 0 files. Evidence against my own hypothesis: 'Iwakuni' IS a normal row of the PlaceNames blob, sitting in a run of real Japanese cities (Hofu / Iwakuni / Kudamatsu / Mine / Nagato), so its presence in the blob is innocent -- but a blob row does not need to be an AS3 string constant. Separately confirmed and NOT in doubt: the web pool's namestarting and nameending runs match the android arrays in order and content with exactly the two absences a deduplicating pool predicts (Kiyo once instead of twice; 'i' and 'no' deduped), so the generator TABLES are cross-build consistent. Closing this needs a web-side NameGenerator decompile, which the repo does not hold.
text: The web v0.717 build may carry a third hardcoded territory-name exception ('Iwakuni') that the Android v0.682 getPlaceName does not, which would make the ported name generator emit the wrong name for at least one territory.

text: The world map bitmap is IN the repo and is byte-checkable — nobody has cited it. reference/extracted/android/110_Mobile_MapBitmapData.bin is a 272-byte GIF89a, 63 x 72, with exactly 735 non-black pixels. Applying QuestEngine.processMapBitmapData's transform to all 735 gives territoryx in [329,389], territoryy in [291,360], and mapid in [1347935, 1593647]. The '735 territories' figure is therefore MEASURED, not inferred, and the entire world grid can be generated deterministically from a 272-byte artifact already on disk.
